title: Semantic Density: Uncertainty Quantification for Large Language Models through Confidence Measurement in Semantic Space
abstract: With the widespread application of Large Language Models (LLMs) to various domains, concerns regarding the trustworthiness of LLMs in safety-critical scenarios have been raised, due to their unpredictable tendency to hallucinate and generate misinformation. Existing LLMs do not have an inherent functionality to provide the users with an uncertainty/confidence metric for each response it generates, making it difficult to evaluate trustworthiness. Although several studies aim to develop uncertainty quantification methods for LLMs, they have fundamental limitations, such as being restricted to classification tasks, requiring additional training and data, considering only lexical instead of semantic information, and being prompt-wise but not response-wise. A new framework is proposed in this paper to address these issues. Semantic density extracts uncertainty/confidence information for each response from a probability distribution perspective in semantic space. It has no restriction on task types and is "off-the-shelf" for new models and tasks. Experiments on seven state-of-the-art LLMs, including the latest Llama 3 and Mixtral-8x22B models, on four free-form question-answering benchmarks demonstrate the superior performance and robustness of semantic density compared to prior approaches.

claims.text: Semantic Density achieves higher AUROC scores than six baseline UQ metrics across 26 out of 28 model-dataset evaluations on four free-form question-answering benchmarks.
Semantic Density achieves higher average AUPR scores than six baseline UQ metrics across 27 out of 28 model-dataset evaluations on four free-form question-answering benchmarks.
The performance improvements of Semantic Density over alternative UQ metrics are statistically significant with p-values below 10^-6 in paired t-tests.
Semantic Density retains reliable AUROC performance when using as few as four reference responses.
Semantic Density achieves higher AUROC scores than baseline UQ metrics in 6 out of 7 open-source LLMs on the DUC-2004 single-document summarization task.
Semantic Density estimates response confidence by combining length-normalized LLM output probabilities with NLI-based contextual semantic distance expectations via a dimension-invariant kernel.

limitations.text: Semantic Density requires access to the output token probabilities generated by the LLM, which may not be exposed by certain proprietary black-box API models.
The experimental evaluation was primarily limited to sentence-level response generations rather than direct long-paragraph generation.
Semantic entropy is prompt-wise rather than response-wise and relies on binary one-cut semantic equivalence without accounting for fine-grained semantic distance.
Supervised fine-tuning or classifier-based UQ approaches require task-specific ground-truth confidence labels and model-specific training.

future_work.text: Develop new sampling strategies that explicitly encourage better coverage of the semantic space for generating reference responses.
Develop text embedding methods capable of measuring contextual semantic similarity between responses more reliably.
Design specialized kernel functions tailored specifically to capture semantic relationships in semantic space efficiently.
Extend Semantic Density to long multi-paragraph responses by decomposing text into sentence-level claims or factoids.

methodologies.name: Semantic Density Framework
methodologies.description: An off-the-shelf, response-wise uncertainty quantification method that estimates probability density in continuous semantic space using kernel functions over NLI-derived contextual distances weighted by LLM sequence probabilities.
conditions: 7 LLMs: Llama-2-13B, Llama-2-70B, Llama-3-8B, Llama-3-70B, Mistral-7B, Mixtral-8x7B, Mixtral-8x22B
Temperature scaling applied to token probabilities during postprocessing (temperature=0.1)
